dashboard.label: Get Data In — Overview
dashboard.description: The ways to get data into Splunk, and which are live in this lab.

html.p: New to Splunk? Before Splunk can search or visualize anything, the data has to arrive. There are a few common ways to bring it in — this app demonstrates each one:

ul.li: Syslog — devices/servers stream their logs to Splunk over the network (push). Already live here from the Ubuntu hosts and the Splunk server.
REST / API polling — Splunk periodically pulls data from a system's API. Here we poll the Proxmox virtualization API every 60s.
SSH — Splunk logs into a device (e.g. a Cisco router), runs commands (license, certificates, NTP), and indexes the output.
SNMP — poll network devices for interface/health metrics (via Splunk Connect for SNMP).
SOAP — an older XML web-service style; parked for now.

html.p: Under the hood, the pull-based methods (REST, SSH, SNMP) use Splunk scripted/modular inputs: a small script Splunk runs on a schedule whose output becomes events.
